title: Count complete instrument failures by groups rather than by scalar readings
statement: Under exactly G=2f+1 separately counted instrument groups, each reporting pairwise differences, universal recovery against f entirely bad groups requires and is ensured by connectedness of every group subgraph. Hence G*(n-1) scalar outputs are necessary; for n12,f2,G5, five11-output reference stars attain55scalars using5vector calls.

body: Every nontrivial source cut must be crossed by at least2f+1 distinct groups, or split the crossing groups into two f-sized fault sets and confuse shifted potentials. With exactly2f+1 groups, each group must therefore cross every cut and be connected. Conversely each healthy connected group supplies a correct path difference and their median is correct. The source explicit counterexample puts all five root-incident edges of the30-edge graph into one instrument: a1/100 root shift becomes indistinguishable after just that one group fails. This refutes importing the edge theorem into the different fault-count grammar, while leaving the edge theorem valid. Five group calls return55scalars, not5scalar observations. No probabilistic iid assumption or universal arbitrary-sensor55bound is asserted.
